summary: Referencing a missing attribute such as `result.exists` instead of `result.stat.exists` was hidden by the `false` test in older versions; it now raises an error.
questions: Why does failed_when: result.exists is false now error?
How do I check if a file exists using a registered stat result?
Why was my failed_when never true in older Ansible?

answer_card.title: Fix references to missing attributes like result.exists
answer_card.answer_md:
This task references a non-existent attribute. The `false` test silently ignored the undefined value, so the condition could never be true:

```yaml
- stat:
    path: /does-not-exist
  register: result
  failed_when: result.exists is false
```

ansible-core 2.19 reports an error. Use the `stat` key:

```yaml
  failed_when: result.stat.exists is false
```
